title: Titans-like surprise-gated long-term memory with shared Mirror basis
hypothesis: A shared value basis plus per-key codes can compress surprise-gated long-term memory while preserving recall; private residual rank identifies where sequence-specific value directions are needed. Short-term cache state is measured and charged separately.
physical_object: One shared long-term value basis plus per-key writable memory codes
mirror_coordinate: Per-key code selecting shared value directions, with optional private residual code
logical_multiplicity: 64 key-value long-term memories with an 8-entry short-term cache

task.metric: Long-term-only and cache-aware query MSE/Gaussian NLL, surprise-triggered writes, full serialized state bytes

controls: Full Titans-like writable long-term matrix plus short-term cache
Shared rank-4 long-term value basis only
Shared basis plus private value residual rank r
Native low-rank basis/code memory with identical decoder

storage.authority: actual serialized inference and memory-state payload bytes

success_gate: For at least one r on both development seeds, complete memory payload <=50% of full-matrix control and cache-aware query MSE <=1.10x full control; report private-rank frontier. Mirror-specific success additionally requires a strict gain over native low-rank memory control.
failure_gate: No quality/storage point meets gate or exact native low-rank alias without a Mirror-specific gain. Fresh seeds remain sealed.
boundaries: Titans-inspired surprise-gated fast-weight memory, not a paper reproduction
One-hot synthetic keys and linear value retrieval
Short-term cache is identical and separately charged for all methods
No neural memory network or language-model claim
